The Edit permission was denied, so I made no change. I did not try another route to write the file.

**Baseline** (from `/home/kobii/missions/s4-fixtures/harness-target/.claude/settings.json`; there is no `/harness-audit` here)
- The file is valid JSON (`python3 -m json.tool` passes).
- It is the only file in `.claude/`.
- It has one hook group, `PostToolUse`, with two entries. Both match `Edit` and run the same command: `bash -c 'echo edited $(cat) >> /tmp/edits.log'`.
- The two entries are identical, so every edit fires the hook twice. The log gets two lines per edit.
- The two hooks run with the same hook input, so each should read the same stdin. I did not confirm how Claude Code runs duplicate hooks, so I can't say whether the second one sees an empty stdin.

**Proposed change** (not applied)
- Delete the second, duplicate `PostToolUse` entry (line 5) in `.claude/settings.json`, and remove the trailing comma on line 4.
- It is reversible, stays inside `.claude/`, and leaves `src/` untouched.
- To validate it, run `python3 -m json.tool` on the file and check that `hooks.PostToolUse` has exactly one entry.
- To apply it, grant Edit permission on that path and re-dispatch me. You can also delete the line by hand.

**Remaining risks**
- The hook logs raw tool input (`$(cat)`) to `/tmp/edits.log`. That file is world-readable and could pick up file contents or secrets.
- The command has no error handling and an unquoted `$(cat)`. Multi-line input gets collapsed and is subject to word splitting.
- The `Edit` matcher skips `Write`, `MultiEdit` and `NotebookEdit`, so those changes are never logged.
- `/tmp/edits.log` has no rotation and no size cap.
- Nothing in `.claude/` covers permissions, deny rules or a test or eval hook.
- The `bash -c` quoting works on Linux and macOS but is fragile on Windows, which matters for cross-platform use.
